title: Multi-Aspect Indexing
summary: Index different views of the same source so queries can match its content, purpose, entities, and structure without losing source identity.
overview: Multi-aspect indexing creates several retrieval representations for one source object. A technical document may have body-text embeddings, a concise summary, extracted questions, a title vector, and structured entity fields. Each representation emphasizes a different route by which users describe the same evidence.

These views should converge on one authoritative source identity and revision. Generated summaries or questions can improve discovery but must not become independent evidence. Combining aspects requires calibrated fusion and deduplication; otherwise documents with more representations receive an unfair ranking advantage simply because they appear more often.

production.poc: A prototype compares body-only retrieval with one additional aspect on labeled query types.
production.production: Production versions every derived view, records source lineage, and evaluates whether each aspect contributes unique relevant hits.
production.scale: At scale, control indexing fan-out, rebuild all dependent aspects on source changes, and monitor representation-specific drift and storage cost.

components.name: Source registry
components.role: Assigns stable document and revision identifiers across all views.

components.name: Aspect builders
components.role: Generate body, title, summary, question, or entity representations.

components.name: Multi-vector index
components.role: Stores aspect-specific vectors and shared metadata.

components.name: Fusion policy
components.role: Combines aspect rankings without counting duplicates as independent evidence.

components.name: Source resolver
components.role: Fetches the authoritative passage behind a matched representation.

flow.title: Choose useful aspects
flow.description: Map observed query patterns to representations with a clear retrieval purpose.

flow.title: Build derived views
flow.description: Generate each aspect from the same approved source revision.

flow.title: Index with lineage
flow.description: Store aspect type, embedding version, source identity, and access metadata.

flow.title: Search relevant aspects
flow.description: Dispatch only the views appropriate to the query under a bounded budget.

flow.title: Fuse by source
flow.description: Combine rankings and deduplicate at the authoritative document or passage level.

flow.title: Fetch real evidence
flow.description: Supply source text rather than generated index summaries as the basis for factual answers.

useCase.title: Finding evidence across varied report language
useCase.situation: Underwriters search inspection reports by property feature, risk question, or report title.
useCase.problem: One body embedding misses queries phrased as underwriting questions rather than report descriptions.
useCase.requirement: Improve discovery while keeping every answer linked to the actual inspection evidence.
useCase.architecture: The index stores body passages, title/entity views, and generated question representations with shared source IDs.
runtime: A query about roof condition matches a generated question view.
The resolver retrieves the original inspection passage and its date before drafting the answer.
useCase.failure: If the generated view invents a property feature, source validation prevents it from supporting the final claim.
useCase.impact: Measure marginal recall from each aspect, duplicate-hit rate, and indexing cost; remove views that add volume without useful retrieval coverage.

tradeoffs.cost: Increase storage, generation, and update cost.
Needs explicit weighting and identity management.

failures.scenario: One aspect remains on an old revision
failures.detection: Search discovers evidence no longer present in the source.
failures.recovery: Invalidate all dependent views and rebuild the revision set.
Treat generated views only as retrieval hints and verify source text.

mistakes.mistake: Counting every view as separate evidence
mistakes.fix: Fuse and deduplicate by authoritative source.
Add views only for measured retrieval gaps.
Track the dependency graph of every derived representation.

whenToUse: Use when users describe the same content in several distinct ways.
Use for structured reports with meaningful titles and entities.
Use when additional views improve measured recall.
whenNotToUse: Avoid many views for already easy exact lookup.
Do not cite generated index text as primary evidence.
checklist: Assign shared source and revision IDs.
Invalidate every view on source change.
Budget indexing cost per source object.
